chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir said:

I asked him about one who forgot to prostrate one prostration, then remembered it while standing. He said: 'He should prostrate it when he remembers, provided he has not yet bowed. If he has already bowed, let him continue with his prayer, and when he finishes, he makes it up, and there is no prostration of forgetfulness (sahw) upon him.'

key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Forgetfulness (specifically referring to the prostration of forgetfulness)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets a prostration during prayer and remembers it while standing?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *sajdah al-ghaflah* (prostration of forgetfulness) and *qada'* (compensation) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that missing a single obligatory prostration does not invalidate the prayer's structure. The hadith establishes that if remembered before *ruku'*, the worshipper returns to complete it in place, whereas remembering after *ruku'* requires completing the prayer and performing the missed prostration separately, without the need for the compensatory prostrations typically associated with general forgetfulness.
